newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
CANADA, April 7 - Montreal, que. - All terminals working normally, with no delays expected.

HONDURAS, April 7 - Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging corn/wheat, 1 discharging bagged urea. 15 Vessels due of which 5 to discharge bananas, 1 passenger vessel. 8 To load/discharge containers, 1 to discharge wheat/sbm. Puerto Cortes - Three vessels berthed, all discharging, of which 2 fertiliser, 1 wheat/corn, 1 vessel anchored, 1 vessel in ballast. 18 Vessels due of which 11 to discharge/load containers/general cargo, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 passenger vessel.

PANAMA, April 7 - Cristobal - 15 Vessels berthed of which 5 operating. Balboa - 14 Vessels berthed of which none operating. Panama Canal - Transit booking system working at full capacity. April 7, 46 vessels due, 19 in queue, 11 booked, 43 scheduled. April 6, actual arrivals 30, transits 33. Average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 16.3 hours.

UNITED STATES, April 7 - Jersey City, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Newark, NJ - Four vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Eight vessels in port. Perth Amboy, NJ - No vessels. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Cartaret, NJ - One vessel in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, with no congestion,delays. Hampton Roads, VA - 11 General cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 5 bulkers berthed loading coal, 1 anchored waiting to load, 1 bulker anchored under attachment. 8 Vessels berthed under repair and/or layberth, 1 bulker anchored waiting to load wood-pulp.Honolulu, HI - Honolulu harbour - 1 Container vessel, 4 tugs and barges berthed. Honolulu anchorage - No vessels. Barbers Point - 2 Barges berthed. Barbers Point offshore mooring - 1 Tanker.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - Dundalk terminal - No congestion anticipated this week. Clear C and D canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Liquid bulk facilities working normally with no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - Vessel traffic expected to be moderate this week at Columbus street terminal. Other terminals working normally. No delays at oil terminals or grain elevator. Miami, FL - Excellent berthing availability at Miami and Port Everglades. Passenger terminals available. The dredging project has been successfully completed, so no more restrictions.

New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, none at container or tanker terminals. Congestion at sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier - 12 Vessels due during this week. At present 2 vessels are anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - 5 Vessels due. At present 1 is waiting to load. Fresh water has now been turned on for the summer at DTR coal terminal, Newport News. Norfolk southern coal pier will undertake scheduled maintenance to the No. 1 ship loading system from 8-29/4. During this period, the No. 1 ship loading system will be out of service. Cargill - No vessels due during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are all working normally. All channels are open with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in the ports of Philadelphia, Camden, or Wilmington. No dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - Garden City terminals are expecting moderate congestion for the coming week. East coast terminal and Ocean terminals are expecting a moderate week, with no delays expected. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility expects long delays. Savannah sugar refinery has barge and one vessel scheduled for the early part of the week but no other vessels scheduled for the remainder of the week. All bulk liquid facilities are operating normally, with no congestion expected. Navigation remains normal. Thunderstorms may cause some downtime on weather sensitive cargoes.

GULF COAST - Houston, Tx - Port congested for vessels requiring open dock. Vessels at berth have been delayed by rain. No congestion at Cargill grain elevator and Houston public elevator. Farmland grain elevator, Galveston is presently congested, with approx. 2-3 days waiting. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains may cause delays in cargo operations, especially grain loading. River stage at 16.5 feet and expected to go down to 16.1 ft. by 7/4. Normal transit times can be expected. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Based on these drafts we advise all vessels to maintain sufficient airdraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river. High river will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 44 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt and 43 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - 14 Grain vessels in port of which 6 loading and 8 waiting. The average waiting period is about 3-6 days. Coos Bay, OR - Working normally. Wood-chip carriers loading at Roseburg dock, lumber vessel loading at export service. Glennbrook nickel terminal busy discharging nickel. Expect activity to increase coming week with two log vessels due, 1 at Ocean terminal the other one to load at Coos Bay dock. Honolulu, HI - Construction has started to repair a damaged mooring dolphin at the pier at the entrance to Honolulu harbour. Ships should use caution wh transiting in and out.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (lb-212-214) - Looks moderate for April. At present, anticipate delays of 1-2 days at anchor awaiting berth. Koch Carbon (lb-211) - At present 4 vessels scheduled April. No berthing delays expected. Kaiser (lr-49) - Looks moderately quite for April. (Coal,petcoke) - No berthing delays expected. April looks quiet for bulk cargoes at Los Angeles and Long Beach harbours. Baltimore, MD - April 8 - Port working normally with 7 bulkers, 4 container vessels, 1 ro-ro, 2 auto vessels, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo vessels, 2 vessels in repair yard. 4 Bulkers awaiting berths of which 2 to discharge sugar, 1 to discharge general cargo, 1 under arrest.
